<!-- Hierarchical regression (DSUJ sections 8.9.1, 8.10 and 8.11), added 2026-10-26 on Johnny's
     request, with the assumption checks of the same model. Uses DSUJ's album sales data with all
     three predictors (datasets/2026/album_sales.csv), so the numbers match Outputs 8.5 to 8.8.
     Needs datasetsPath() from _setup.R, sourced in the "Read data" chunk of
     regression_multiple_predictors.qmd, which runs first. -->

```{r hreg-setup, echo=FALSE}
album <- read.csv(datasetsPath("2026", "album_sales.csv"), check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
m0 <- lm(Sales ~ 1, data = album)
m1 <- lm(Sales ~ Adverts, data = album)
m2 <- lm(Sales ~ Adverts + Airplay + Image, data = album)
nAlbum <- nrow(album)
r2  <- c(0, summary(m1)$r.squared, summary(m2)$r.squared)
k   <- c(0, 1, 3)
df1 <- c(NA, diff(k))
df2 <- nAlbum - k - 1
Fc  <- c(NA, (diff(r2) / diff(k)) / ((1 - r2[-1]) / df2[-1]))
pc  <- c(NA, pf(Fc[-1], df1[-1], df2[-1], lower.tail = FALSE))
f3  <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
fp  <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", f3(p)))
z   <- rstandard(m2)
# Q-Q plot as JASP draws it (same helper as qqJasp() in the lecture 20 wrapper)
qqJasp <- function(res) {
  suppressWarnings(print(jaspGraphs::plotQQnorm(res, yName = "Std. residuals", ablineColor = "darkred",
                                                ablineOrigin = TRUE, identicalAxes = TRUE, ciLevel = 0.95)))
}
```

# Hierarchical regression {.section}

## Isolating individual contributions {.smaller}

- What does a predictor add on top of the others?
- Enter predictors in steps, known ones first (past research)
- $R^2$ change is the extra variance the new predictors explain
- $F$ change tests whether that increase is more than chance

$$F_{change} = \frac{(N - k_{new} - 1)\, R^2_{change}}{k_{change}\, (1 - R^2_{new})}$$

- Album sales (Section 8.10), adding airplay and image to adverts
  - $R^2$ goes from `r f3(r2[2])` to `r f3(r2[3])`, $F$(`r df1[3]`, `r df2[3]`) = `r f3(Fc[3])`, $p$ `r fp(pc[3])`
- [How to in JASP](https://jasp-stats.github.io/jasp-video-library/All_Regression.html#hierarchical-regression)

## Model summary {.smaller}

```{r hreg-model-summary, echo=FALSE}
summaryTable <- data.frame(Model = c("M<sub>0</sub>", "M<sub>1</sub>", "M<sub>2</sub>"),
                           R2 = f3(r2),
                           adjR2 = f3(c(0, summary(m1)$adj.r.squared, summary(m2)$adj.r.squared)),
                           R2change = f3(c(0, diff(r2))),
                           Fchange = c("", f3(Fc[-1])),
                           df1 = c(0, df1[-1]), df2 = df2, p = fp(pc))
knitr::kable(summaryTable, format = "html", escape = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrrr",
             col.names = c("Model", "R<sup>2</sup>", "Adjusted R<sup>2</sup>", "R<sup>2</sup> change",
                           "F change", "df1", "df2", "p"))
```

- $M_1$ includes adverts; $M_2$ includes adverts, airplay and image

## Checking the assumptions {.smaller}

Where to check each assumption in JASP (final model)

::: {style="font-size: 75%;"}
| Assumption | In JASP | Looks fine when |
|------------|---------|-----------------|
| Multicollinearity | Statistics &rarr; Coefficients &rarr; *Tolerance and VIF* | all VIFs below 10, average close to 1 |
| Linearity, equal variances | Plots &rarr; *Residuals vs. predicted* | a random cloud around 0 |
| Normality of the residuals | Plots &rarr; *Q-Q plot standardized residuals* &rarr; *Confidence interval* | points close to the line, mostly within the band |
| Outliers, influential cases | Statistics &rarr; Residuals &rarr; *Casewise diagnostics* | about 5% of std. residuals beyond $\pm 2$ at most, Cook's distance below 1 |
:::

## Residuals of the final model {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
Residuals vs. predicted

```{r hreg-residuals-vs-predicted, echo=FALSE, fig.width=5, fig.height=3.2}
par(cex = 1.3, mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 1, 1))
plot(fitted(m2), z, pch = 21, bg = "grey70", col = "grey30", bty = "n", las = 1,
     xlab = "Predicted sales", ylab = "Std. residuals")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2, lwd = 2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
Q-Q plot standardized residuals

```{r hreg-qq-residuals, echo=FALSE, fig.width=5, fig.height=3.2}
qqJasp(z)
```
:::

::::

- Left plot shows a random cloud around 0, so linearity and equal variances look fine
- Right plot shows points close to the line, so the residuals look normal
